correctness.rationale: A=u phi is rank-one nilpotent precisely when phi(u)=0 and defines an incident projective point/hyperplane flag. For distinct flags commuting cannot have equal nonzero rank-one AB and BA because that would force identical images and kernels, so both cross products vanish iff mutually incident. Degree from Q in H and K through span(P,Q) is T-1, T=a+(a-1)b. Common neighbors of adjacent same-point/hyperplane flags yield a+(b-1)b-2; cross edges yield (q+1)b+(b-q-1)c-2. Their difference q c((q-1)c+1)>0 for n>=4. Such cross edges exist only when two distinct hyperplanes can contain a given line, starting n=4. Multiplying through scalar clique size q-1 gives full matrix-graph profiles. Independent binary n=4 enumeration computed 105 flags, degree 24, and lambda_s=11 vs lambda_c=7 for 630 edges of each cross/same class; n=3 geometry argument checks no cross. Finite instance corroborates uniform proof.

originality.rationale: Boroja–Kokol Bukovšek–Stopar arXiv:2602.07467 Section 5/Theorem 5.1 provides 3x3 finite-field point-line compressed commuting graph and its single same-point/line adjacency. In dimension 4 the mutual point/hyperplane incidence graph has an additional cross edge absent at n=3; exact two local count strata are not implied by the n=3 theorem. Dolinar–Kuzma–Oblak study full commuting graph maximal distances, while Ou–Zhong study upper-triangular rank-one matrices; those differ from the all-rank-one nilpotent induced graph. Resultary semantic search found no exact higher-dimensional flag profile. Higher-rank flag-graph terminology remains an explicit originality risk.
